NameError: name 'plt' is not defined

The chart does not represent the stated scale ablation. It plots only one bar labeled "metrics" with value 90.055, rather than comparing the original scale against scale=0.1 for average accuracy, final accuracy, and forgetting.

The script constructs zero-width confidence intervals by setting ci_low and ci_high equal to the observation. No confidence interval exists because the experiment has one seed; drawing error bars falsely suggests uncertainty was estimated.
The 9 pt title is below the requested 12 pt minimum. Axis labels are 8 pt instead of at least 10 pt, and 7 pt tick labels are likely difficult to read when printed.
The y-axis label "Metric Value (percentage points)" is ambiguous because accuracy and forgetting have different interpretations. Separate panels or clearly grouped metrics are needed.
The x-axis category "metrics" is not a scale setting and conflicts with the x-axis label. Categories should identify the actual scale values, such as original scale and scale=0.1.
Displaying 90.0550 implies unsupported precision for a single-seed smoke run. Two decimal places would be more appropriate.

A single bar cannot communicate an ablation effect. A grouped bar chart with two scale conditions and separate accuracy metrics, plus a distinct forgetting panel, would better match the scientific claim.
The 300 DPI setting is publication-appropriate.
The selected palette is colorblind-safe and avoids default Matplotlib colors, although the current one-bar chart does not meaningfully use the palette.
constrained_layout=True is correctly used, and the light horizontal grid is clean and professional.
Overall quality score too low: 3/10
The figure does not show the specified load-balancing ablation. It contains one bar labeled "metrics" with value 90.055 instead of conditions for weights 0, 0.1, and 1.0.

The accuracy–forgetting trade-off is absent. The plot should show task-0, average, and final accuracy alongside forgetting, preferably using separate aligned panels because forgetting is on a different numerical scale.
Zero-width error bars are drawn by setting both confidence bounds equal to the observation. With one seed, confidence intervals cannot be estimated and error bars should be omitted.
The x-axis label says "Load-Balancing Weight," but the sole tick is "metrics." The ticks should be the evaluated weights 0, 0.1, and 1.0.

The generic y-axis label "Metric Value (percentage points)" obscures the distinction between accuracy levels and forgetting. Separate panels with "Accuracy (%)" and "Forgetting (points)" are recommended.

Axis-label sizes meet the 10 pt requirement, but the 11 pt title is below the requested 12 pt minimum. Tick and legend sizes are acceptable for a double-column figure but should be verified at final print scale.
The label 90.0550 implies unjustified precision for a single-seed, one-epoch smoke result. Two decimal places are sufficient.
No legend is present. A corrected multi-metric chart will require a clearly placed legend outside the plotting area or direct panel labels.
The script correctly uses constrained_layout=True, but the wide 7-by-3-inch canvas is poorly utilized by a single bar.
The colorblind-safe palette, 300 DPI output, white-grid styling, and light horizontal grid are appropriate, but these strengths cannot compensate for the incorrect data mapping.
Overall quality score too low: 3/10
The plotted value is incorrect. The script displays 90.055, which is an accuracy result, rather than the latency values 0.753 ms for sparse Signed Top-2 and 0.533 ms for dense softmax.
The required two-configuration comparison is missing. The chart should contain separate bars for sparse rank-16 Signed Top-2 and dense rank-4 softmax.

The script draws zero-width confidence intervals that were not estimated. Microbenchmark uncertainty should be based on repeated timed runs and shown as standard deviation, interquartile range, or a confidence interval; otherwise error bars must be omitted.
The sole x-axis tick, "metrics," does not identify either routing configuration and makes the chart scientifically uninterpretable.
The 9 pt title is below the required 12 pt minimum, axis labels are 8 pt instead of at least 10 pt, and 7 pt tick labels are unlikely to remain readable at print size.
The long title is likely cramped in a 3.5-inch-wide single-column figure. It should be shortened or wrapped while retaining at least a 12 pt font.

The equal analytical FLOPs value is not represented in the chart. A concise annotation or tick-label qualifier should state that both configurations have 619,773,952 active FLOPs per layer, while the caption retains the parameter-mismatch caveat.
The current four-decimal value label is inappropriate. For the actual measurements, three decimals are justified because the supplied latencies are 0.753 and 0.533 ms.
A legend is unnecessary if the corrected bars have complete x-axis labels. If colors encode sparse versus dense routing, that encoding should remain redundant with the labels.
The 300 DPI setting, constrained layout, colorblind-safe palette, and light horizontal grid are appropriate, but the incorrect data mapping prevents the figure from passing.
Overall quality score too low: 2/10
